Unit 13: Consumerism, Advertising, Branding & Shopping Habits

📚 1. 15 Từ Vựng Cốt Lõi (Kèm Phát Âm Audio Bản Xứ)

⚠️ BẠN ĐANG MỞ Ở CHẾ ĐỘ XEM TRƯỚC — ÂM THANH SẼ KHÔNG CHẠY
Ứng dụng Tệp (Files) và Zalo trên iPhone chặn JavaScript, nên nút 🔊, chấm điểm và micro đều bị vô hiệu.
👉 Hãy mở bài học bằng đường link https:// mà giáo viên gửi (bấm vào link trong Zalo ➔ chọn biểu tượng la bàn Safari).
Bấm để máy tự động đọc lần lượt từng từ và hiển thị theo dõi (phù hợp học trên điện thoại)
1. consumer (n)
/kənˈsjuːmə(r)/
người tiêu dùng, khách hàng mua sắm hàng hóa/dịch vụ
Collocation: modern consumer, consumer behavior, consumer society
"Modern consumers often research product reviews online before making a purchase."
2. commercial (n/adj)
/kəˈmɜːʃl/
(n) quảng cáo trên truyền hình/radio/mạng; (adj) mang tính thương mại
Collocation: television commercial, commercial break, commercial success
"Catchy television commercials can easily influence what young children want to eat."
3. persuade (v)
/pəˈsweɪd/
thuyết phục ai đó làm gì hoặc mua gì (persuade sb to V)
Collocation: persuade consumers to buy, persuasive advertising
"Clever marketing campaigns persuade people to upgrade their smartphones every year."
4. endorse (v)
/ɪnˈdɔːs/
đại diện quảng cáo, bảo chứng thương hiệu (thường do người nổi tiếng thực hiện)
Collocation: endorse a product, celebrity endorsement
"Sports brands pay millions of dollars to famous athletes who endorse their running shoes."
5. celebrity (n)
/səˈlebrəti/
người nổi tiếng, ngôi sao giải trí/thể thao
Collocation: popular celebrity, celebrity culture, celebrity endorsement
"Many teenagers buy cosmetics simply because their favorite celebrity uses them."
6. impulse (n)
/ˈɪmpʌls/
sự bốc đồng, ngẫu hứng tức thời (mua hàng không có kế hoạch trước)
Collocation: buy on impulse, impulse buying, impulse purchase
"Flash sales on shopping apps encourage customers to buy unnecessary items on impulse."
7. brand (n)
/brænd/
thương hiệu, nhãn hàng
Collocation: global brand, brand awareness, luxury brand
"Building a trustworthy brand requires consistent product quality and honest service."
8. loyalty (n)
/ˈlɔɪəlti/
lòng trung thành (của khách hàng với một thương hiệu)
Collocation: brand loyalty, customer loyalty, build loyalty
"Supermarkets offer membership points to build long-term customer loyalty."
9. manipulate (v)
/məˈnɪpjuleɪt/
thao túng, dẫn dắt tâm lý một cách tinh vi
Collocation: manipulate public opinion, manipulate emotions
"Critics argue that some advertisements manipulate people's insecurities to sell beauty products."
10. target (v/n)
/ˈtɑːɡɪt/
nhắm mục tiêu vào một nhóm khách hàng cụ thể
Collocation: target young audiences, target market
"Fast-food companies should not be allowed to target commercial campaigns at young children."
11. trend (n)
/trend/
xu hướng, trào lưu tiêu dùng hoặc thời trang
Collocation: fashion trend, consumer trend, set a trend
"Social media influencers play a major role in setting fast-fashion trends."
12. luxury (n/adj)
/ˈlʌkʃəri/
sự xa xỉ; hàng hiệu cao cấp đắt tiền
Collocation: luxury goods, luxury brand, live in luxury
"Some consumers spend a large proportion of their income on luxury handbags and watches."
13. affordable (adj)
/əˈfɔːdəbl/
có giá cả phải chăng, hợp túi tiền
Collocation: affordable price, affordable clothing
"Most families prefer durable household appliances sold at an affordable price."
14. boycott (v/n)
/ˈbɔɪkɒt/
tẩy chay, ngừng mua hàng để phản đối hành vi sai trái của doanh nghiệp
Collocation: boycott a company, consumer boycott
"Environmentally conscious citizens often boycott brands that pollute local rivers."
15. ethical (adj)
/ˈeθɪkl/
có đạo đức, minh bạch và có trách nhiệm với xã hội/môi trường
Collocation: ethical advertising, ethical consumerism
"Ethical companies ensure that their factory workers receive fair remuneration and safe conditions."

⚙️ 2. Bài Giảng Ngữ Pháp 2 Tầng (Grammar Masterclass)

🟢 Tầng 1: Câu Điều Kiện Loại 2 (Second Conditional — Giả Định Không Có Thật Ở Hiện Tại)

• Công thức chuẩn: If + S + V2/ed (were cho mọi ngôi), S + would / could / might + V (nguyên mẫu)
  - Dùng để bàn luận về các giả định chính sách hoặc tình huống trái ngược với thực tế hiện tại trong IELTS Writing Task 2 & Speaking Part 3.
  Ví dụ 1: If governments banned junk-food commercials aimed at children, childhood obesity rates would decline significantly.
  Ví dụ 2: If I were a wealthy celebrity, I would only endorse ethical and eco-friendly brands.

🔵 Tầng 2: Cấu Trúc Động Từ Tác Động Tâm Lý (Verb + Object + To-Infinitive) & Bị Động

• Chủ động: persuade / encourage / tempt / lead / manipulate + Object (tân ngữ) + to V
  Ví dụ: Flash-sale notifications tempt consumers to buy luxury items on impulse.

• Bị động học thuật (Nâng GRA lên Band 7.0+): be persuaded / be tempted / be manipulated + to V
  Ví dụ: Teenagers are easily persuaded to purchase trendy clothes endorsed by famous celebrities.

🎯 20 Câu Test Từ Vựng (Vocabulary Mastery Test)

1. Smart ________ always compare prices and quality before buying electronic devices.
2. Many parents complain that there are too many toy ________ on television during weekend cartoons.
3. Emotional storytelling is a powerful marketing tool used to ________ customers to try a new product.
4. Famous football players are paid millions of pounds to ________ sportswear and energy drinks.
5. When a popular ________ wears a jacket on social media, it often sells out within hours.
6. Placing chocolates near the supermarket checkout counter encourages shoppers to buy them on ________.
7. Apple and Samsung are two of the most recognizable technology ________ in the world.
8. Excellent after-sales service helps companies build strong customer ________ over many years.
9. Dishonest advertisements try to ________ viewers by making exaggerated promises about weight loss.
10. Energy drink manufacturers often ________ their online advertisements at teenagers and gamers.
11. Following every short-lived fashion ________ can waste a lot of money and create textile pollution.
12. Designer handbags and Swiss watches are examples of ________ goods that symbolize social status.
13. Public universities should provide high-quality education at an ________ tuition fee for all students.
14. Consumers threatened to ________ the clothing company after discovering it used child labor.
15. ________ advertising provides truthful product information without deceiving vulnerable buyers.
16. [Ôn tập Unit 12] Impulse buying on credit cards can quickly ruin a family's monthly ________.
17. [Ôn tập Unit 12] During the holiday sale season, online shopping expenditure ________ dramatically.
18. [Ôn tập Unit 11] Skilled marketing specialists who design successful campaigns often earn a rapid ________.
19. [Ôn tập Unit 9] Local authorities must ________ commercial billboards near historic temples.
20. [Ôn tập Unit 3] Buying fewer fast-fashion clothes helps reduce industrial ________ and waste.

⚙️ 10 Câu Test Ngữ Pháp Ứng Dụng (Grammar Mastery Test)

1. If governments ________ deceptive commercials aimed at children, parents would face less pester power.
2. If I ________ a famous athlete, I would never endorse unhealthy sugary drinks or fast food.
3. Social media algorithms persuade young consumers ________ trendy items they do not actually need.
4. Consumers would develop stronger brand loyalty if companies ________ more honest about product quality.
5. During online flash sales, millions of shoppers are tempted ________ luxury gadgets on impulse.
6. If every citizen ________ unethical brands that pollute the environment, corporations would change their practices.
7. Bright packaging and free toys are designed to encourage children ________ their parents for fast food.
8. Many people ________ save a larger proportion of their income if they uninstalled shopping apps from their phones.
9. Celebrity endorsements often lead teenagers ________ that expensive luxury goods bring happiness.
10. Advertising agencies ________ manipulate consumers' fears should be fined heavily by the government.

Tốc độ đọc:
Trạng thái: Sẵn sàng phát Câu: 0 / 15
💡 Bấm vào bất kỳ câu thoại nào để nghe riêng câu đó:
👩 Market Researcher: Excuse me! We are conducting a short consumer behavior survey for the City Retail Association.
👨 Shopper: Sure, I have a few minutes before my train leaves. Happy to help!
👩 Market Researcher: Thank you! First, could you tell me your surname? Is it spelled Fletcher?
👨 Shopper: No, it is Thornton. That is spelled T - H - O - R - N - T - O - N. 💡 Đáp án câu 1 (Đánh vần họ): THORNTON
👩 Market Researcher: Got it, Mr. Thornton. When you buy electronics or clothes, what influences your decision the most?
👨 Shopper: I never trust television commercials or celebrity endorsements. I always read independent customer reviews. 💡 Đáp án câu 2: customer reviews / reviews
👩 Market Researcher: Interesting. Have you ever bought something on impulse during an online sale?
👨 Shopper: Yes, last month a pop-up advertisement persuaded me to buy a smart coffee maker on impulse. 💡 Đáp án câu 3 (Món đồ mua ngẫu hứng): coffee maker
👩 Market Researcher: How much did you spend on that impulse purchase?
👨 Shopper: It was originally £120, but with a discount voucher I paid £85. 💡 Bẫy giá gốc vs giá thực trả câu 4: 85
👩 Market Researcher: What factor builds your long-term loyalty to a clothing brand?
👨 Shopper: For me, ethical production and affordable prices are much more important than a luxury logo. 💡 Đáp án câu 5: ethical production / affordable prices
👩 Market Researcher: Would you ever boycott a famous brand?
👨 Shopper: Definitely. I boycott any company that tests cosmetics on animals or pollutes the environment. 💡 Đáp án câu 6: animals
👩 Market Researcher: Thank you very much, Mr. Thornton! Here is a £10 book token for completing our survey.
Điểm: 0/6

📰 IELTS Academic Reading: Passage & Questions

[Paragraph A - From Information to Emotional Manipulation]
In the past, advertisements simply informed the public about the features and affordable price of a new product. Today, however, global corporations spend billions of dollars on sophisticated commercials designed to manipulate human emotions. Instead of selling a physical item, marketing agencies sell a lifestyle. By hiring a famous celebrity to endorse a perfume or sports car, companies persuade millions of fans that buying a luxury brand will bring them instant social status.

[Paragraph B - Targeting Vulnerable Audiences and Impulse Buying]
Digital technology has made advertising even more powerful because social media platforms track every user's browsing history. Algorithms can target personalized advertisements at teenagers who want to follow the latest fashion trend. Countdown timers and 'limited stock' warnings are deliberately used to trigger impulse buying, tempting consumers to purchase clothes and gadgets they do not genuinely need.

[Paragraph C - The Rise of Ethical Consumerism]
Fortunately, modern shoppers are becoming more aware of these marketing tactics. Rather than showing blind brand loyalty, educated citizens increasingly demand ethical business practices. If a corporation is caught damaging the environment or exploiting workers, consumers can organize an online boycott within hours. Consequently, honesty and sustainability are becoming essential for long-term commercial survival.
Điểm: 0/6
